title: SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son Explored $1 Trillion Moonshot Buyout of SK Hynix
author: F
text:
S

soAsian
Well-known member

SoftBank Group Chief Executive Masayoshi Son sounded out Wall Street financial institutions about financing a potential $1 trillion takeover of South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter. A SoftBank spokesperson told the publication that the company was no longer actively considering the acquisition.

SK Hynix told Reuters it had no knowledge of the matter and said any foreign acquisition would require advance approval from the South Korean government. It remains unclear whether SoftBank approached SK Hynix or its largest shareholder, SK Square, or whether any financial institution was prepared to back the proposed purchase.

The price alone would have posed a formidable hurdle. SK Hynix was worth about $577 billion at Friday’s close, according to Aju Press, putting the reported $1 trillion figure roughly 73% above its market value. SoftBank also has substantial capital committed to OpenAI, adding to the challenge of financing a transaction of that size.

The strategic appeal was access to high-bandwidth memory, which lets AI accelerators move large volumes of data quickly. SK Hynix supplies that memory to Nvidia and competes with Samsung Electronics and Micron Technology. As demand for advanced AI chips has grown, memory suppliers have become more important to the companies designing accelerators and building data centers to run them.

For SoftBank, owning a major memory producer would have extended its reach across the AI supply chain. The Japanese group already controls Arm, whose chip designs underpin a range of processors, and has invested heavily in OpenAI. SK Hynix would have added large-scale semiconductor manufacturing to that portfolio. The financing inquiry shows how far Son was prepared to look for a foothold in AI memory, even as the cost and need for government approval made a takeover difficult to execute.
